name: instatus
description: Check, post and update incidents, maintenance, components and subscribers on your Instatus status pages.

interface.longDescription:
Run your Instatus status page from the chat where you're handling the incident. Ask what's broken and why a monitor is failing, measure uptime for a period, see what went down and for how long, post and update incidents, schedule maintenance, put up general notices, see who's on call and acknowledge a page, and manage components and subscribers.

When you connect you choose read only or read and write, and all projects or only the ones you pick. Both are enforced by Instatus, not by the assistant. Every post says whether subscribers are notified, and nothing is sent to them unless you ask for it. If an incident with the same title is already open on the same components, a new one is refused and the open one is shown instead.

The assistant works as you, with the same projects and permissions you have in the Instatus dashboard. Setup and details: https://instatus.com/help/mcp
defaultPrompt: Is anything broken on my status page, and why?
What was our uptime last month?
Post an incident: API errors in Europe, don't notify subscribers yet

positive.description: Check the current state of a status page
positive.prompt: Is anything broken on my Instatus status page right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the user's status page and reports its overall status, any affected components, and any open incidents or running maintenance.

positive.description: Open an incident without notifying subscribers
positive.prompt: Open an incident on my status page: the API is returning errors in Europe. Mark the API as partial outage and don't notify subscribers.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a published incident with the API component in partial outage, reports the incident link, and says subscribers were not notified.

positive.prompt: Schedule maintenance on the database component next Sunday from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC, without notifying subscribers.
positive.expected_behavior: Schedules a two-hour maintenance window on the database component for next Sunday and confirms it without notifying subscribers.

positive.description: Explain why a monitor is down
positive.prompt: Why is the payments webhook monitor failing, and since when?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the monitor, reads its latest checks and reports the HTTP status, the locations that failed and when the failures started, without changing anything.

positive.prompt: What was the uptime of our monitors in October?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports uptime, estimated downtime and response times per monitor for October, and says if a monitor has no data for part of the month.

negative.description: Third-party service status, not the user's own page
General writing with no status page action
negative.prompt: Write a short apology email to a customer about yesterday's outage.
How do I create a status page in Atlassian Statuspage?

publication.release_notes: First release: check what's broken and why a monitor is failing, measure uptime, post and resolve incidents, schedule maintenance, post general notices, see who's on call and acknowledge pages, and manage components and subscribers on Instatus status pages.
